description: We are interested in bettering our communities and our world by developing cutting edge software solutions for astronauts!
summary:
VITALIS is a free, browser-based health monitoring tool that helps astronauts assess their own health on long-duration missions. Astronauts log eight indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep, mood and exercise. Each reading is colour-coded green, amber or red against reference ranges. A clickable body map shows brain, heart, metabolism, immune system, and bones and muscles at a glance. Trend charts and a full history table reveal slow changes, and plain-language guidance explains how to measure each indicator, why spaceflight affects it, what to do next, and when to contact flight surgeons.

Environment settings for a space station, deep-space transit, a lunar base and a Mars base change exercise targets, priority checks and advice, including a warning about communication delays with Earth. Daily tasks, points and streaks keep crews engaged.

This matters because on long missions, such as a trip to Mars, help from Earth is delayed and astronauts must catch problems like bone loss, cardiovascular strain, immune changes and declining mood early. VITALIS runs offline, keeps data on the device, and needs no setup.
details:
What it does and how it works
VITALIS is a single-page web app that runs entirely in the browser. An astronaut enters daily readings for heart rate, blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), blood sugar, body temperature, sleep, mood and exercise. Each value is checked against a healthy range and a caution range, then shown as green (in range), amber (watch) or red (act now). The app calculates a crew health score and highlights the matching region on a clickable body map: brain (sleep, mood), heart (heart rate, blood pressure), metabolism (blood sugar), immune system (temperature) and bones and muscles (exercise). Selecting an indicator shows how to measure it, why spaceflight affects it, what to do at each status, and when to contact flight surgeons. Line charts with the healthy range shaded, trend arrows and a history table show slow changes that a single reading would miss. A “Load 14-day demo” button fills in sample data so reviewers can see every feature immediately.

Benefits and intended impact
On long missions help from Earth is delayed, so astronauts need to spot problems early on their own. VITALIS turns raw numbers into clear status colours and next steps, so the user doesn’t need medical training to interpret them. It works offline, installs nothing, and keeps all data on the device, making it highly practical for actual usage in space. VITALIS is intended to ensure astronaut health, even if astronauts aren't health specialists themselves.

Tools used
HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no external libraries, SVG for the body map, the HTML canvas for charts, and browser local storage for saved data. It is hosted on Netlify. Claude (an AI assistant by Anthropic) was used to assist in writing the code.

Creativity
The body map groups regions by the indicators they cover, and the immune system is shown as a whole-body outline because it isn’t one organ. The environment selector actually changes the guidance, and gamification is tied to health behaviours. These are all examples of our creativity.

Factors considered
The five spaceflight hazards (radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, gravity and closed environments), simple language for non-experts, mobile and offline use, and privacy.

Limitations
The reference ranges are general adult guidelines, and the exercise targets and priority lists are design assumptions. VITALIS is an educational prototype, not a diagnostic tool, and the demo data is simulated.
